Gene Description

SYK is a cytoplasmic non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase with tandem SH2 domains that recognize phosphorylated immune-receptor signaling motifs. Receptor recruitment and autophosphorylation activate SYK, which phosphorylates adaptor and enzyme substrates and also supplies docking interfaces for sustained signaling complexes. It is central to B-cell antigen-receptor, Fc-receptor, C-type lectin and integrin-linked signaling. Context-dependent roles extend to myeloid cytokine responses, platelet activation, receptor trafficking, microglial lipid responses and epithelial signaling. SYK can also phosphorylate Ikaros on serine residues in a defined regulatory context. Its effects on cytokines, adhesion and cell survival depend on receptor, cell type and stimulation, rather than having one universal sign.

Summary: The Reactome negative inflammatory-response branch is compatible with inhibitory immune-receptor signaling and with source-specific opposing SYK effects in TLR pathways.
Reason: The original Reactome FCGR3A-mediated IL10 synthesis pathway supports a context-specific anti-inflammatory output of immune-receptor signaling. SYK executes proximal phosphorylation in this cytokine-producing route, rather than acting as IL10 itself. PMID:23962979 independently illustrates opposing, stimulus-specific SYK effects in TLR pathways; it is corroboration of context dependence, not an experiment on the FCGR3A branch. Retain negative inflammatory regulation as non-core, not a universal anti-inflammatory function.

Purified full-length enzyme in PMID:10648173 and native human B-cell enzyme in PMID:8163536 establish the reaction independently of domain/ancestral mappings. PMID:18818202 directly distinguishes ITAM binding and autophosphorylation as activation mechanisms. Membrane recruitment is peripheral and does not confer receptor-spanning topology; the varied original substrate/pathway citations retain their own assay contexts. The preserved original source is PMID:28386764.

Summary: SYK phosphorylates Ikaros and thereby promotes its nuclear accumulation; it is not demonstrated to carry Ikaros through the pore as an import receptor.
Reason: SYK phosphorylates Ikaros and thereby promotes its nuclear accumulation; it is not demonstrated to carry Ikaros through the pore as an import receptor. Refine the role to positive regulation of protein import into nucleus, supported by SYK knockdown and Ikaros phosphosite/phosphomimetic mutants. This is a lateral role correction, not a claim that the regulatory term is a descendant of nuclear import. The preserved original source is PMID:23071339.
Proposed replacements: positive regulation of protein import into nucleus

Core Functions

ATP-dependent non-receptor tyrosine phosphorylation transmits BCR, Fc-receptor, C-type lectin and integrin-linked signals to adaptor and enzyme substrates. Activation can arise through ITAM engagement or autophosphorylation, and substrate choice depends on the signaling assembly.

Molecular Function:
non-membrane spanning protein tyrosine kinase activity
Directly Involved In:
B cell receptor signaling pathway Fc-epsilon receptor signaling pathway Fc-gamma receptor signaling pathway involved in phagocytosis stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway integrin-mediated signaling pathway
Cellular Locations:
cytosol plasma membrane
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:10648173
    specific tyrosine phosphorylation of a Syk peptide substrate
  • PMID:8163536
  • PMID:15509800
  • PMID:18818202
  • PMID:19358895

Tandem SH2 domains recognize phosphotyrosine-containing receptor motifs and couple membrane recruitment to activation; SYK phosphotyrosines separately recruit other SH2-containing proteins to sustained signaling assemblies.

Molecular Function:
phosphotyrosine residue binding
Cellular Locations:
plasma membrane
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:9698567
    tandem SH2 domain of Syk complexed with a dually phosphorylated ITAM peptide
  • PMID:7761456

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(SYK-notes.md)

Complete BCR-panel reassessment, 2026-10-26

All baseline rows were manually assessed, including roles outside BCR signaling. The original term, reference, evidence, partner, isoform, qualifier and NOT payloads remain unchanged. No new annotation was added; mouse Syk retains its two historically inherited NEW rows. Actual Falcon/fallback and publication-retrieval jobs were run by the shared acquisition workflow. Provider failures were recorded honestly; provider prose is not used as primary evidence. Normal additional publication recovery and direct source inspection resolved the principal catalytic and binding claims. Incomplete source access remains explicit in individual review reasons rather than being converted into wrong-gene or negative-function conclusions.

The principal molecular activity is non-receptor tyrosine phosphorylation with tandem-SH2-mediated phosphotyrosine recognition. A broad kinase assertion is refined to supported chemistry rather than removed. Cytoplasm is retained alongside finer pools, and membrane recruitment does not imply integral membrane topology. Binding to a phosphotyrosine ligand is distinguished from binding to another protein's SH2 domain. Purified recombinant and mixed-species DT40 complementation assays retain their construct species; DT40 host identity does not identify every tested protein.

Primary PMID:10648173 and 8163536 establish human tyrosine kinase activity, while 18818202 separates ITAM binding and autophosphorylation. The structural tandem-SH2 work (9698567/7761456) supports the binding core. Full PMID:23071339, recovered normally from PMC because the PMID extraction omitted key sections, directly assays Ikaros serine phosphorylation: mapped mouse Ikaros S358/S361 correspond to human S361/S364. Human-cell knockdown supports the native substrate response. Serine kinase activity and Ikaros-dependent transcription are retained as contextual, and nuclear import is corrected laterally to positive regulation of import rather than assigning SYK the import-carrier role.

Full PMID:31875558 explicitly says “LACC1 did not associate with either Dectin-1 or Syk”; the preserved positive LACC1 interaction is contradicted within its source. Other bare-binding rows are removed only under the information-content rule, or refined when exact partners support kinase, phosphatase, scaffold, phosphotyrosine or transcription-factor binding. Unknown screen pairs remain unresolved. The STAT3 mechanism has independent direct support (20133729), so an abstract foregrounding another partner is not grounds to remove an otherwise established function.

The normal publisher page for 32514138 exposes Extended Data Figure 4a: human iMG cells respond to PS liposomes with SYK phosphorylation. That figure supports lipid response, not a resolved binary SYK–PLCG2 interaction. Independent full 27609517 does test PLCgamma2 tandem-SH2 binding to Syk, weaker than PLCgamma1. The 22267217 abstract and figure headings describe a caspase-8 inflammasome, not enough to settle an apoptotic-process claim; 27477018's exact SYK clearance experiment remains access-limited. These are specific uncertainties, not claims that SYK is uninvolved.

Native human neutrophil adhesion/chemotaxis (12885943), immune-receptor phosphorylation and mouse ortholog developmental/myeloid studies retain their respective scopes. Reactome FCGR3A-mediated IL10 synthesis supports one anti-inflammatory context; the TLR study 23962979 corroborates opposing pathway effects without being treated as a direct FCGR3A experiment.

id: P43405
gene_symbol: SYK
product_type: PROTEIN
status: COMPLETE
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: SYK is a cytoplasmic non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase with tandem SH2 domains that recognize
  phosphorylated immune-receptor signaling motifs. Receptor recruitment and autophosphorylation activate
  SYK, which phosphorylates adaptor and enzyme substrates and also supplies docking interfaces for sustained
  signaling complexes. It is central to B-cell antigen-receptor, Fc-receptor, C-type lectin and integrin-linked
  signaling. Context-dependent roles extend to myeloid cytokine responses, platelet activation, receptor
  trafficking, microglial lipid responses and epithelial signaling. SYK can also phosphorylate Ikaros
  on serine residues in a defined regulatory context. Its effects on cytokines, adhesion and cell survival
  depend on receptor, cell type and stimulation, rather than having one universal sign.

  review:
    summary: SYK directly phosphorylates proteins, while the cited SLP65 reconstitution study additionally
      resolves a kinase-independent adaptor role.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: SYK directly phosphorylates proteins, while the cited SLP65 reconstitution study additionally
      resolves a kinase-independent adaptor role. Keep the broad phosphorylation process because both
      tyrosine and contextual serine substrate chemistry are experimentally supported; do not reduce all
      SYK function to its adaptor effect or to one phosphorylation class. The preserved original source
      is PMID:17681949.

- term:
    id: GO:0006606
    label: protein import into nucleus
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:23071339
  qualifier: acts_upstream_of_or_within
  review:
    summary: SYK phosphorylates Ikaros and thereby promotes its nuclear accumulation; it is not demonstrated
      to carry Ikaros through the pore as an import receptor.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: SYK phosphorylates Ikaros and thereby promotes its nuclear accumulation; it is not demonstrated
      to carry Ikaros through the pore as an import receptor. Refine the role to positive regulation of
      protein import into nucleus, supported by SYK knockdown and Ikaros phosphosite/phosphomimetic mutants.
      This is a lateral role correction, not a claim that the regulatory term is a descendant of nuclear
      import. The preserved original source is PMID:23071339.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:23071339
    - reference_id: url:https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3497833/
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0042307
      label: positive regulation of protein import into nucleus

- id: PMID:19136564
  title: Phospholipase Cgamma2 is critical for Dectin-1-mediated Ca2+ flux and cytokine production in
    dendritic cells.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The mouse donor PMID:19136564 tests Dectin-1-dependent dendritic-cell activation and
      its signaling effectors. Human Dectin-1/SYK inhibition in PMID:19358895 independently supports activation
      in immune cells. Cell activation is as broad as these multiple cellular outputs warrant, and is
      retained as contextual biology rather than made the defining molecular function. SYK transmits signals
      from stimulatory C-type lectin receptors through phosphorylated receptor/adaptor motifs to downstream
      enzymes. Human dendritic-cell inhibitor experiments in PMID:19358895 and native mouse Dectin-1 studies
      independently support the catalytic signaling role. The BCR is not its only receptor context. SYK
      transmits signals from stimulatory C-type lectin receptors through phosphorylated receptor/adaptor
      motifs to downstream enzymes. Human dendritic-cell inhibitor experiments in PMID:19358895 and native
      mouse Dectin-1 studies independently support the catalytic signaling role. The BCR is not its only
      receptor context. The preserved original source is PMID:19358895. Native mouse Dectin-1 experiments
      and human Candida/beta-glucan perturbation establish SYK-dependent cellular responses to fungal
      material and lectin-receptor engagement. Retain these stimulus-specific outcomes outside the molecular
      core, without making SYK the extracellular fungal-ligand-binding receptor.
- id: PMID:12522250
  title: Regulation of blood and lymphatic vascular separation by signaling proteins SLP-76 and Syk.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The source mouse knockout study PMID:12522250 demonstrates defective blood–lymphatic
      separation and hematopoietic dependence, not a requirement for SYK expression in every endothelial
      cell. Retain the human orthology-based vascular-development role with that source-specific cellular
      boundary; a conserved immune kinase does not by itself prove native human endothelial action. The
      original mouse knockout paper PMID:7477352 exposes perinatal bleeding and lymphocyte-development
      defects in the accessible abstract, but not the exact organ-morphogenesis experiment behind this
      human TAS. Independent vascular-network evidence supports a narrower developmental context, not
      every organ. Preserve uncertainty about this broad citation-specific claim rather than infer a wrong-gene
      error or invent an organ assay. The preserved original source is PMID:7477352.
- id: PMID:22078883
  title: CD14 controls the LPS-induced endocytosis of Toll-like receptor 4.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Native mouse studies identify SYK–PLCgamma2 signaling in CD14-dependent TLR4 endocytosis
      (PMID:22078883) and SYK-dependent CD36 internalization (PMID:23395392). These support conserved
      receptor-trafficking and associated interferon responses in human as orthology inferences, not direct
      human experiments for every receptor. IFN effects depend on cell type and stimulus, as the dendritic-cell
      results in PMID:26708990 show.

      and native mouse Dectin-1 studies independently support the catalytic signaling role. The BCR is
      not its only receptor context. SYK participates catalytically in innate leukocyte receptor responses,
      including Dectin-1-dependent cytokine signaling and integrin-dependent antimicrobial functions.
      Native mouse genetics and human dendritic-cell perturbation support these broad immune-context claims;
      they are not evidence that every immune output has the same direction. SYK transmits signals from
      stimulatory C-type lectin receptors through phosphorylated receptor/adaptor motifs to downstream
      enzymes. Human dendritic-cell inhibitor experiments in PMID:19358895 and native mouse Dectin-1 studies
      independently support the catalytic signaling role. The BCR is not its only receptor context. The
      preserved original source is PMID:19358895. The mouse Dectin-1 study PMID:15845454 identifies early
      phagosome-associated SYK signaling; conserved receptor recruitment supports the human transfer.
      This is a peripheral signaling pool at the developing phagosome, not constitutive luminal residency.
      Positive IL10 regulation is directly demonstrated for the Dectin-1/SYK pathway in native mouse dendritic
      cells in PMID:15845454. Human PMID:19358895 supports the same receptor/kinase response but its abstract

- id: PMID:19797524
  title: Neutrophil-specific deletion of Syk kinase results in reduced host defense to bacterial infection.

  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM

    review_notes: SYK participates catalytically in innate leukocyte receptor responses, including Dectin-1-dependent

- id: PMID:9171347
  title: The Fc receptor gamma-chain and the tyrosine kinase Syk are essential for activation of mouse
    platelets by collagen.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The mouse donor PMID:9171347 shows loss of collagen-induced secretion and aggregation
      in Syk-deficient platelets, while thrombin responses persist. Human platelet SYK association/activation
      and GPVI studies independently support conserved platelet signaling. Retain the specified output
      as a contextual inference, without asserting that SYK synthesizes serotonin/arachidonate or controls
      every platelet agonist. SYK executes a receptor-proximal kinase step in collagen/GPVI platelet activation.
      Human platelet studies and mouse genetics support this Reactome pathway context; the reaction is
      not universally required for thrombin-triggered activation.
- id: PMID:23962979
  title: The tyrosine kinase Syk differentially regulates Toll-like receptor signaling downstream of the
    adaptor molecules TRAF6 and TRAF3.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The original Reactome FCGR3A-mediated IL10 synthesis pathway supports a context-specific
      anti-inflammatory output of immune-receptor signaling. SYK executes proximal phosphorylation in
      this cytokine-producing route, rather than acting as IL10 itself. PMID:23962979 independently illustrates
      opposing, stimulus-specific SYK effects in TLR pathways; it is corroboration of context dependence,
      not an experiment on the FCGR3A branch. Retain negative inflammatory regulation as non-core, not
      a universal anti-inflammatory function.
- id: url:https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3497833/
  title: Serine phosphorylation by SYK is critical for nuclear localization and transcription factor function
    of Ikaros
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PMID:23071339 directly tests purified recombinant SYK phosphorylation of Ikaros, with
      phospho-amino-acid analysis and mass spectrometry, and native human-cell knockdown supports regulation
      of Ikaros. The mapped mouse Ikaros S358/S361 correspond to human S361/S364; this is genuine serine
      phosphorylation by SYK, not merely activation of a downstream serine kinase. Retain this contextual
      chemistry alongside its principal tyrosine kinase function. The preserved original source is PMID:23071339.
      PMID:23071339 examines SYK–Ikaros in human cells and supports a nuclear as well as cytoplasmic pool.
      Retain contextual nuclear localization rather than exclude it because receptor signaling is mainly
      cytoplasmic. Nuclear localization of Ikaros is a separate substrate response. The preserved original
      source is PMID:23071339. Human-cell SYK depletion reduces native Ikaros nuclear localization, DNA
      binding and target-gene expression in PMID:23071339. Retain downstream transcriptional regulation
      in this substrate-specific context; SYK supplies phosphorylation, not sequence-specific DNA recognition
      or RNA polymerase catalysis. The preserved original source is PMID:23071339. SYK phosphorylates
      Ikaros and thereby promotes its nuclear accumulation; it is not demonstrated to carry Ikaros through
      the pore as an import receptor. Refine the role to positive regulation of protein import into nucleus,
      supported by SYK knockdown and Ikaros phosphosite/phosphomimetic mutants. This is a lateral role
      correction, not a claim that the regulatory term is a descendant of nuclear import. The preserved
      original source is PMID:23071339.
